'''Alexander Angus MacFarlane-Grieve''',  {{Post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|sep=,|MC|TD}} (11 May 1891 – 2 August 1970) was a British academic, mathematician, [[Rowing (sport)|rower]], and decorated [[British Army]] officer. He served with the [[Highland Light Infantry]] during [[World War I]]. He was [[Master (college)|Master]] of [[University College, Durham]] from 1939 to 1954, and additionally Master of [[Hatfield College, Durham]] from 1940 to 1949.<ref name="obit - Times">{{cite news|title=Col. Macfarlane-Grieve|work=The Times|issue=57934|date=3 August 1970|page=8}}</ref><ref name="bio - Durham Castle Society">{{cite web|title=Lt-Col Angus Alexander Macfarlane-Grieve|url=https://www.castlealumni.uk/history/masters/macfarlane-grieve|website=History|publisher=Durham Castle Society|accessdate=8 August 2015}}</ref>

==Early life==
MacFarlane-Grieve was born on 11 May 1891,<ref name="obit - Times" /> and was [[baptised]] at [[St Mary Abbots]], an [[Anglican]] church in [[Kensington]], London.<ref name="bio - Clan MacFarlane Genealogy">{{cite web|last1=Lythgoe|first1=Darrin|title=Maj. Angus MacFarlane-Grieve, of Edenhall & Pencrise Peel|url=http://www.clanmacfarlanegenealogy.info/genealogy/TNGWebsite/getperson.php?personID=I5749&tree=UL|website=Clan MacFarlane Genealogy|accessdate=8 August 2015}}</ref> He was educated at [[The Perse School]], a [[Private schools in the United Kingdom|private school]] in [[Cambridge]], England.<ref name="obit - Times" /> He went on to study [[mathematics]] at [[University College, Durham]], and graduated with a Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree in 1913.<ref name="bio - Durham Castle Society" /> He [[Rowing (sport)|rowed]] for both his college ([[University College Boat Club (Durham)|University College Boat Club]]) and for the university ([[Durham University Boat Club]]).<ref name="obit - Times" /> He was President of the DUBC during his final year, from 1912 to 1913.<ref name="obit - Times" />

==Military service==
On 15 August 1914, having been a member of the [[Officer Training Corps]] while at university, MacFarlane-Grieve was commissioned into the 4th Battalion, [[The Highland Light Infantry]], [[British Army]], as a [[second lieutenant]] (on probation).<ref name="LG 8 September 1914">{{London Gazette |issue=28894 |date=8 September 1914 |pages=7100–7101  |}}</ref> In December 1914, his commission and rank were confirmed.<ref name="LG 8 December 1914">{{London Gazette |issue=29002 |date=8 December 1914 |page=10574 |supp=y |}}</ref> In July 1915, he attended the Scottish Command School of Signalling at [[Peebles]], Tweeddale, Scotland.<ref>{{cite web|title=MIA 2/27|url=http://reed.dur.ac.uk/metsnav/vu/navigate.do?oid=http://endure.dur.ac.uk:8080/fedora/get/UkDhU:MIA_2/METS&pn=27&size=full|website=Photograph albums of A. A. MacFarlane-Grieve|publisher=Durham University Library|accessdate=8 August 2015}}</ref> He then became one of three officers commanding the 4th Battalion's signal section.<ref>{{cite web|title=MIA 2/34|url=http://reed.dur.ac.uk/metsnav/vu/navigate.do?oid=http://endure.dur.ac.uk:8080/fedora/get/UkDhU:MIA_2/METS&pn=34&size=full|website=Photograph albums of A. A. MacFarlane-Grieve|publisher=Durham University Library|accessdate=8 August 2015}}</ref> By June 1917, he had been promoted to [[Captain (British Army and Royal Marines)|captain]].<ref name="Edinburgh Gazette - 1 June 1917">{{cite news|title=The Silver Medal for Valour |url=https://www.thegazette.co.uk/Edinburgh/issue/13098/page/1034 |accessdate=8 August 2015 |work=The Edinburgh Gazette |issue=13098 |date=1 June 1917|pages=1032–1034}}</ref> By the end of the war, he held the [[acting rank]] of [[Lieutenant colonel (United Kingdom)|lieutenant colonel]].<ref name="Eve">{{cite web |title=Item of the Month - On the eve of war: the University College 1914 Shooting Eight |url=https://www.dur.ac.uk/palace.green/whatshere/iotm/archive/2014/06/ |website=Palace Green Library Exhibitions |publisher=Durham University |access-date=24 November 2020 |date=June 2014}}</ref>

On 4 August 1923, he was transferred to the Regular Army Reserve of Officers (thereby ending his army career) and was promoted to [[Major (United Kingdom)|major]] with seniority from 4 May 1922.<ref name="LG 3 August 1923">{{London Gazette |issue=32850 |date=3 August 1923 |page=5342 |}}</ref> While an academic at Durham, he was an officer of the Durham University contingent of the Officer Training Corps.<ref name="LG 23 February 1932" />

==Academic career==
In 1923, having left the army, MacFarlane-Grieve returned to [[Durham University]] to become a lecturer in military subjects.<ref name="bio - Durham Castle Society" /> Between 1923 and 1939, he was also [[Bursar]] of [[University College, Durham]].<ref name="bio - Hatfield">{{cite web|title=Principals & Masters: Angus Macfarlane-Grieve|url=http://community.dur.ac.uk/hatfield.history/intour/masters.htm|website=Hatfield College History|publisher=Durham University|accessdate=10 August 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140814150425/http://community.dur.ac.uk/hatfield.history/intour/masters.htm|archive-date=14 August 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 1939, at the age of 47, he was appointed [[Master (college)|Master]] of University College.<ref name="obit - Times" /><ref name="bio - Durham Castle Society" /> He was the first head of the college not to be not in [[Holy Orders]]: i.e. he was the first [[layman]].<ref name="obit - Times" /> With [[World War II]] causing a shrinkage in student numbers, he was additionally appointed acting Master of [[Hatfield College, Durham]] in 1940. He stood down from that acting appointment in 1949 and was succeeded by [[Eric Birley]].<ref name="bio - Hatfield" /> From 1948 to 1953, he was Sub-Warden of the Durham Colleges and therefore the deputy of the [[List of Vice-Chancellors and Wardens of the Durham University|Vice-Chancellor and Warden]] with specific responsibility for the [[Colleges of Durham University]].<ref name="obit - Times" /><ref name="bio - Durham Castle Society" />

In 1953, MacFarlane-Grieve inherited the [[family estate]] at [[Edenhall]], [[Scottish Borders]], and retired early from Durham.<ref name="bio - Hatfield" />

==Honours==
In May 1917, MacFarlane-Grieve was awarded the [[Silver Medal of Military Valor]] by the [[King of Italy]] "for distinguished services rendered during the course of the campaign".<ref name="Edinburgh Gazette - 1 June 1917" /> In June 1917, he was awarded the [[Military Cross]] (MC) "for distinguished service in the field".<ref name="LG 1 June 1917">{{London Gazette |issue=30111 |date=1 June 1917 |pages=5468–5481  |supp=y |}}</ref> In February 1932, he was awarded the [[Efficiency Decoration]] (TD) for long service.<ref name="LG 23 February 1932">{{London Gazette |issue=33801 |date=23 February 1932 |page=1216 |}}</ref>
